body:
Flagged by AI reviewer in PR #1824.

## Problem

`dev/dev-poll.sh` treats a non-dev label (`issue_is_dev_claimable`, including a hand-applied `awaiting-live-verification`) as a skip, but the skip does not leave the in-progress scan.

Around lines 789–793 the scan logs "skipping" and sets `OTHER_AGENT_INPROGRESS=true`. It does not `continue`. The assignee block immediately below (around line 797) still runs. If that issue is assigned to `$BOT_USER`, dev-poll spawns `dev-agent.sh` (review fix, CI fix, or stale-branch / post-crash recovery) anyway.

The later stale-sweep block (around line 901) is gated on `OTHER_AGENT_INPROGRESS=false`, so only the unassigned path is actually skipped. A self-assigned in-progress issue that a human labelled `awaiting-live-verification` — the remaining use of that label after #1804 — is not left alone.

`AGENTS.md` says dev-poll skips `awaiting-live-verification`. The comment above the check (issue #608) says dev-poll must only touch issues it could claim.

## Failure mode

Hand-label an open, bot-assigned, `in-progress` issue `awaiting-live-verification`. The next dev-poll tick can relaunch dev-agent on it.

---
*Auto-created from AI review*

## Affected files

- `dev/dev-poll.sh` (in-progress scan, non-dev label skip)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An open, `$BOT_USER`-assigned `in-progress` issue with a non-dev label (e.g. `awaiting-live-verification`) is left alone by the next dev-poll tick — no `dev-agent.sh` spawn (review-fix, CI-fix, or stale-branch/post-crash recovery paths do not run for it)
- [ ] The non-dev-label skip in the in-progress scan now `continue`s out of the loop instead of only setting OTHER_AGENT_INPROGRESS=true
- [ ] Existing stale-sweep behaviour for unassigned in-progress issues is unchanged

Flagged by AI reviewer in PR #1809.

## Problem
The stale "Not the runtime yet: docker-compose.yml is still the factory's live stack until cutover." header remains in these Nomad jobspecs (PR #1809 fixed only edge.hcl):
- nomad/jobs/forgejo.hcl:30
- nomad/jobs/staging.hcl:16
- nomad/jobs/agents-dev-qwen.hcl:46
- nomad/jobs/agents-review-qwen.hcl:46
- nomad/jobs/agents-supervisor-opus.hcl:28
- nomad/jobs/woodpecker-server.hcl:30

The production factory (disinto-nomad-box) runs the Nomad+Vault backend (docs/updating-factory.md), and `disinto init --backend=nomad --with <svc>` deploys each jobspec via lib/init/nomad/deploy.sh, so "until cutover" is no longer true. An agent trusting these headers might edit the generated docker-compose.yml / docker/Caddyfile instead of the Nomad job when making service changes — the same failure mode as #1779, which PR #1809 fixed for edge.hcl.

---
*Auto-created from AI review*

## Affected files

- `nomad/jobs/forgejo.hcl`
- `nomad/jobs/staging.hcl`
- `nomad/jobs/agents-dev-qwen.hcl`
- `nomad/jobs/agents-review-qwen.hcl`
- `nomad/jobs/agents-supervisor-opus.hcl`
- `nomad/jobs/woodpecker-server.hcl`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The stale header "Not the runtime yet: docker-compose.yml is still the factory's live stack until cutover." is removed from all six jobspecs listed
- [ ] No live jobspec still carries the "until cutover" claim (grep across nomad/jobs/ shows none)
- [ ] Jobspecs are unchanged except for the stale comment (no behavioural change)

Flagged by AI reviewer in PR #1805.

## Problem

PR #1760 / #1805 stops `docs/agents-llama.md`, `docs/nomad-migration.md`, and `docs/updating-factory.md` from restarting or running the stopped all-roles `agents` job (`nomad/jobs/agents.hcl`, #1522). Two operator checklists still treat that job as the live agents job:

- `disinto-factory/setup.md` line 353, Nomad "Watch it work": `nomad job status agents`
- `disinto-factory/operations.md` lines 14–15, "Check factory status": `nomad job status agents` and `nomad job inspect agents -json | jq '.Allocations[] | ...'`

On the production box that job is stopped. An operator following either checklist sees a dead job and can conclude the agents are down, while the live per-role `agents-*` jobs are running. `operations.md` already says "There is no job named agents" a few lines later, so the two sections contradict each other.

Related stale reference, same root cause: `INFRASTRUCTURE.md` attributes the `agent-data` and `project-repos` host volumes only to `nomad/jobs/agents.hcl`. The live per-role jobs mount those volumes; the stopped all-roles job does not.

`disinto init --backend=nomad --with agents` still submits `nomad/jobs/agents.hcl` on a fresh box, so a status example must not hardcode `agents` or hardcode only the production per-role names. Query whichever `agents*` jobs are running, the same way #1760 does.

## Failure mode

Copy-paste of the setup/operations Nomad checklist reports the factory agents as dead when they are not.

---
*Auto-created from AI review*

## Affected files

- `disinto-factory/setup.md` (Nomad "Watch it work", ~line 353)
- `disinto-factory/operations.md` ("Check factory status", lines 14-15)
- `INFRASTRUCTURE.md` (agent-data / project-repos volume attribution)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] setup.md "Watch it work" and operations.md "Check factory status" no longer hardcode `nomad job status agents` / `nomad job inspect agents` — they query the running agents* jobs (same approach as #1760)
- [ ] INFRASTRUCTURE.md no longer attributes the agent-data and project-repos host volumes only to the stopped nomad/jobs/agents.hcl
- [ ] The two operations sections no longer contradict each other

Flagged by AI reviewer in PR #1816.

## Problem

`docs/edge-routing-fallback.md` is a contingency plan, but several claims no longer match the code (pre-existing; #1798 only removed chat from the plan):

- Lines 108–110 say `do_register()` currently creates a single route and that the fallback would need to register three routes, and tell the reader to see the TODO in `tools/edge-control/register.sh`. There is no TODO in that file. In `EDGE_ROUTING_MODE=subdomain`, `do_register()` already adds `forge.<project>` and `ci.<project>` beside the main route (`tools/edge-control/register.sh`).
- The "Files to Change on Pivot" table says `tools/edge-control/lib/caddy.sh` still needs `add_route()` subdomain support. `add_route()` already treats its first argument as a host label and appends `DOMAIN_SUFFIX`, which is how subdomain routes are registered today.
- "New Environment Variables (pivot only)" says `EDGE_TUNNEL_FQDN_FORGE` / `EDGE_TUNNEL_FQDN_CI` would be added to the edge service environment block (line ~415). They are already emitted by `lib/generators.sh` (around lines 682–683). `_generate_caddyfile_subdomain` already writes the three host blocks.
- Cited line numbers are stale: `_generate_caddyfile_impl` is around line 825, not ~596; `EDGE_TUNNEL_FQDN` is around line 678, not ~432.

An operator following this plan would look for work that is already done and for a TODO that does not exist.

---
*Auto-created from AI review*

## Affected files

- `docs/edge-routing-fallback.md` (single-file doc correction)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The do_register() description matches current code (it already adds forge.<project> and ci.<project> beside the main route; the non-existent TODO in register.sh is removed or reworded)
- [ ] The "Files to Change on Pivot" table reflects current state (add_route() already handles host-label + DOMAIN_SUFFIX subdomain routes; EDGE_TUNNEL_FQDN_FORGE / EDGE_TUNNEL_FQDN_CI are already emitted by lib/generators.sh)
- [ ] Stale line-number citations are corrected or removed (e.g. _generate_caddyfile_impl ~line 825 not ~596; EDGE_TUNNEL_FQDN ~line 678 not ~432)
